title: Capture orders from the job queue with retries

pr.title: Add the capture-order job with gateway retries
pr.description:
Adds the `capture-order` job. It charges the order total with the card gateway and marks the order paid or declined.

A timeout or a 502, 503, or 504 answer gets more attempts with the shared retry policy (`PAYMENT_RETRY_ATTEMPTS`, `PAYMENT_RETRY_BASE_MS`). The new `retry()` helper is generic, so the refund job can use it in a follow-up. When the last attempt fails, the order goes back to pending and the job queue runs the job again later.

Tests cover the paid, declined, retried, and failed paths with a fake gateway.

bugs.note: Non-idempotent retry: each attempt sends a new randomUUID() idempotency key. The unchanged gateway.ts says that a GatewayTimeout can follow a created charge and that only a repeated key prevents a second charge, so a retried timeout, and each later run of the failed job, charges the card again. subscriptions.ts shows the stable key.

Callee contract in an unchanged file: gateway.charge() resolves a decline with status "declined" and never throws CardDeclined (only authorize() does). captureOrder does not check charge.status, so a declined card marks the order paid with the ID of the declined charge. The fake gateway of the tests throws CardDeclined, so the tests pass.

traps.why: The status check and markCapturing look like a check-then-act race between two workers, but the unchanged markCapturing() is one conditional UPDATE that throws OrderBusy when another worker moved the order first, and the unchanged worker.ts marks such a job done.
The exponential wait has no cap, but the unchanged config.ts limits maxAttempts to 1 to 5 and baseDelayMs to 50 to 2000, so the longest wait is 16 s in a background job.
The audit write looks like a floating promise that can reject unhandled, but the unchanged AuditLog.record() catches every error and never rejects, by its contract.
